summary: Extracts typed context values from dictionaries or Pydantic models, preserves Boolean absence during expression binding, and validates caller-supplied batch identity before backend conversion or chunking.
lifecycle_notes: extract_context_values resolves metadata context fields, normalizes missing/None to a typed NOT_SET sentinel (None for bool), and otherwise preserves the supplied value.
_context_literal and _nullable_bool preserve null Boolean inputs through backend casts; the nullable wrapper is used only where Boolean absence needs an explicit expression type.
_validate_context_ids verifies the field name and existence, then aggregates total/non-null/distinct counts in one query. A single null ID is invalid even if distinctness would pass.

ExpressionRulesEngine calls identity validation on the full submitted relation in _prepare_contexts before its chunk loop. BatchRuleResult.unmatched_context_ids uses it separately on the original submitted contexts.
risks: Leading-underscore helpers are shared across modules: filter.engine imports all four; batch_result imports _validate_context_ids only. Internal names still require coordinated caller changes.
ID validation is global before chunking, not a uniqueness check within each independent chunk. Chunking therefore does not eliminate the full-input identity scan.
extract_context_values normalizes None, not arbitrary invalid or NaN values; do not infer broader normalization guarantees from typed missing-value handling.

evidence.detail: Missing-context semantics, policy/output schema restrictions, batch identity and input boundaries are documented in the current source checkout; source bodies are authoritative.
